stories.title: OPEN Impact, JLL Partner to Lease Up BankNote Building
stories.excerpt: OPEN Impact Real Estate and JLL have been retained to lead leasing and marketing efforts at the historic BankNote Building in the Bronx, one of New York City’s leading destinations for nonprofit, educational and public-sector organizations. The assignment, which will be led by OPEN co-founder Stephen Powers and JLL Vice Chairman Mitchell L. Konsker, marks the latest chapter in the evolution of the approximately 405,000-square-foot property. Once an industrial landmark, the building has grown into one of the Bronx’s largest hubs for nonprofit organizations, government agencies, educational institutions and other mission-driven enterprises. “There are very few opportunities in New York City where you can find this combination of scale, character, infrastructure and mission,” said Powers. “The BankNote Building has always been about more than real estate. It has evolved into a place where organizations serving New Yorkers can work alongside one another and amplify their impact. We’re excited to help shape what comes next.” The post OPEN Impact, JLL Partner to Lease Up BankNote Building appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: OPEN Impact and JLL retained to lease 405K SF BankNote Building in Bronx
Historic industrial property converted to hub for nonprofits, government, educational tenants
Mission-driven organizations anchor demand for affordable, character-rich office space
stories.summary: OPEN Impact Real Estate and JLL have been engaged to lead leasing and marketing for the approximately 405,000-square-foot BankNote Building in the Bronx, a repurposed industrial landmark now serving as a hub for nonprofit organizations, government agencies, and educational institutions. The property has evolved into one of the borough's largest centers for mission-driven enterprises. The assignment signals continued institutional appetite for mission-aligned office consolidation in affordable, accessible Bronx submarkets.
stories.impact: Institutional leasing momentum in the Bronx's nonprofit corridor demonstrates stable demand for affordable office space tethered to employment clusters. This anchors multifamily demand from mission-sector workers who typically earn stable but moderate wages—a persistent renter cohort. The scale and stability of mission-tenant portfolios can support nearby workforce housing development, particularly in East Bronx submarkets where proximity to major employers justifies new supply.

stories.title: JLL Arranges $50M Bridge Loan for Thousand Oaks R&D and Office Campus
stories.excerpt: JLL’s Capital Markets group arranged $49.75 million in bridge financing for Lakeview Innovation Center, an approximately 275,000-square-foot, 100% leased, R&D and office campus in Thousand Oaks. The group worked on behalf of Alta West to secure the three-year, floating-rate financing with Forbright Bank. Alta West Partners acquired Lakeview Innovation Center as a value-add investment opportunity at 50% leased in September 2024. Over the past 24 months, Alta West executed a successful business plan, bringing the property to full occupancy. JLL’s Capital Markets Debt Advisory team representing the borrower was led by senior managing director Jeff Sause, director Josh Blank, senior managing director Marc Schillinger, director Alex Olson, associate Jalynn Borders and analyst Danny Ryan. “This execution is the result of the amazing transformation Alta West has achieved at this asset,” said Blank. “They recognized the potential and have delivered significant value creation by securing long-term deals with high-caliber tenants that raise the profile of the asset.” The post JLL Arranges $50M Bridge Loan for Thousand Oaks R&D and Office Campus appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Alta West closed $49.75M bridge loan at Lakeview Innovation Center, Thousand Oaks
275K SF R&D/office campus fully leased after 24-month value-add repositioning
Forbright Bank financed 170% NOI growth through tenant placement and capex
stories.summary: Alta West Partners secured a $49.75 million three-year floating-rate bridge loan from Forbright Bank for Lakeview Innovation Center, a fully leased 275,000-square-foot R&D and office campus on 22 acres in Thousand Oaks, Ventura County, California. Alta West acquired the property at 50% occupancy in September 2024 and executed a value-add business plan achieving full occupancy and delivering more than 170% NOI growth. Tenants include Marvell, LabCorp, Rawlings Sporting Goods, and Anchor Loans, along with luxury amenities such as Equinox, a café, and pickleball courts.
stories.impact: Forbright's willingness to finance a fully leased, recently stabilized R&D campus at tight terms signals continued capital appetite for life-sciences and tech-oriented office in Southern California submarkets despite broader office headwinds. Ventura County's continued attraction of semiconductor, biotech, and logistics tenants reinforces jobs-in-place demand for both workplace proximity and residential supply; Thousand Oaks and surrounding submarkets remain underserved for workforce multifamily relative to employment concentration. Developers should assess land and development sites within commute shed of these innovation corridors.

stories.title: NYCHA Cuts Ribbon on $636M Rehab of East Brooklyn Apartments
stories.excerpt: The New York City Housing Authority (NYCHA) and Reid Park Rock PACT Partners, which includes Fairstead, BRP Companies, Urbane and the Local Development Corporation of East New York, today were joined by residents and elected officials at a ribbon-cutting ceremony marking the completion of the $636-million rehabilitation of Reid & Park Rock homes in East Brooklyn. Renovations at Reid & Park Rock, formerly the Reid Apartments and Park Rock Consolidated developments, were completed through NYCHA’s Permanent Affordability Commitment Together (PACT) program. The rehabilitation modernized 1,696 affordable homes across 87 buildings, delivering interior and exterior apartment upgrades, building system improvements, enhanced security measures and expanded resident services for nearly 3,000 residents. “The $636-million rehabilitation of Reid & Park Rock is an impressive achievement in the scale and breadth of improvements delivered through NYCHA’s PACT program,” said NYCHA EVP and chief real estate officer Heather Beck. “This project has again demonstrated how comprehensive investments through the PACT program can strengthen not just the buildings but the long-term well-being of the people who call them home.” The post NYCHA Cuts Ribbon on $636M Rehab of East Brooklyn Apartments appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: NYCHA completed $636M rehab of Reid & Park Rock homes in East Brooklyn
1,696 units across 87 buildings modernized through PACT program partnerships
Fairstead, BRP, Urbane, and LDC of East New York delivered affordability preservation
stories.summary: The New York City Housing Authority (NYCHA) and Reid Park Rock PACT Partners, including Fairstead, BRP Companies, Urbane, and the Local Development Corporation of East New York, completed a $636 million comprehensive rehabilitation of Reid & Park Rock homes in East Brooklyn. The project modernized 1,696 affordable units across 87 buildings, delivering interior and exterior upgrades, building system improvements, security enhancements, and expanded resident services for nearly 3,000 residents. The work was executed through NYCHA's Permanent Affordability Commitment Together (PACT) program.
stories.impact: The Reid & Park Rock stabilization removes a major supply-side uncertainty in East Brooklyn's rental market and locks in 1,696 units of permanent affordability for decades, reducing competition pressure on nearby private market rents in the submarket. However, the $636M public-sector commitment and long-term affordability guardrail may suppress private multifamily development ROI in adjacent East Brooklyn/Canarsie submarkets, as investors will face headwinds competing against improved, permanently affordable public housing. Developers should focus on market-rate or workforce-targeted development (140%–160% AMI) in nodes outside the immediate PACT footprint to avoid direct subsidy-anchored competition.

stories.title: Anaheim Sale is First Closing in Broader Multifamily Portfolio
stories.excerpt: Marcus & Millichap recently completed the sale of Empire Apartments, a 29-unit multifamily property in Anaheim. The property sold for $8.5 million, or $293,103 per unit. “This transaction was completed all cash and non-contingent at signing, with a 26-day escrow,” said Tyler Leeson, executive managing director investments. “It also represents the first closing from a broader Anaheim-area multifamily portfolio the seller is repositioning as part of a 1031 exchange strategy into apartment properties elsewhere in Orange County. We remain positive on the market as well-located properties with renovation and operational upside continue to draw buyer demand.” Leeson, Drew Holden, Matt Kipp and Nick Kazemi, of The Leeson Group in Marcus & Millichap’s Orange County office, marketed the property on behalf of the seller, a family that had owned the property for more than 30 years. They also procured the buyer, a large property management company. Built in 1964, Empire Apartments is located at 1215 S. Empire St. The buyer plans to modernize unit interiors as they turn. The post Anaheim Sale is First Closing in Broader Multifamily Portfolio appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Empire Apartments, 29-unit Anaheim property sold for $8.5M ($293K per unit), all-cash
26-day escrow; seller repositioning portfolio via 1031 exchange into Orange County
Buyer is property management company planning unit interior modernization
stories.summary: Marcus & Millichap closed the sale of Empire Apartments, a 29-unit multifamily property in Anaheim, for $8.5 million, or $293,103 per unit. The transaction was completed all-cash and non-contingent at signing with a 26-day escrow. The sale represents the first closing from a broader Anaheim-area multifamily portfolio the seller, a family owner for 30+ years, is repositioning through a 1031 exchange strategy into apartment properties elsewhere in Orange County. The buyer, a large property management company, plans to modernize unit interiors.
stories.impact: The rapid all-cash close at $293K/unit signals continued investor appetite for value-add small-to-mid-cap multifamily in Orange County submarkets despite higher interest-rate environment. The seller's 1031 exchange repositioning into 'apartment properties elsewhere in Orange County' suggests capital flowing from older, less-competitive vintage stock toward newer or better-positioned assets, likely in higher-barrier-to-entry coastal or master-planned submarkets. Developers should monitor if this 1031 pattern accelerates—capital recycling from secondary Orange County product can lower acquisition costs for land banks while tightening valuations in prime development zones (Irvine, Newport Beach, Costa Mesa), raising entry costs and reducing feasibility of new-build deals in premium locations.

stories.title: Personal Training Studio LIV Method Takes 12K SF in Meatpacking District
stories.excerpt: The LIV Method, a private luxury training and wellness studio, will open a new location in Manhattan’s Meatpacking District in January, Commercial Observer has learned. The studio, which offers customers a curated and personalized approach to training, wellness and longevity, has inked a 12,028-square-foot lease at Sage’s 2 Gansevoort Street, according to the landlord. The new location will be LIV Method’s third Manhattan studio. “The LIV Method is exactly the type of experience we envisioned bringing to 2 Gansevoort,” Michael Lenchner, executive vice president and director of leasing at Sage, said in a statement. “It is a luxury offering that is highly personal, hospitality-driven and focused on the complete experience. For our tenants and members, it adds another exceptional wellness resource to the property, while its broader neighborhood access makes 2 Gansevoort an even more dynamic destination within the Meatpacking District.” The asking rent and length of the lease were not provided. The average asking rent for retail space in the area near Washington Street and 14th Street was $333 per square foot during the third quarter of 2026, according to CBRE data. LIV will occupy space across two levels that will be connected by an open staircase. The location will provide fitness and personal training services, a sauna, a cold plunge, massage services and IV wellness treatments. “We are creating a luxury environment with beautiful finishes, exceptional hospitality and highly individualized programming, but the experience is designed to feel welcoming and personal,” Matt Sauerhoff, CEO and founder of LIV Method, said in a statement. “Everyone who walks through our doors should feel that the space was created specifically for them. After nearly three years on the Upper East Side, we’re excited to bring that same tailor-made experience to 2 Gansevoort and the Meatpacking District.” LIV’s Upper East Side spot is at 157 East 86th Street. bullets: LIV Method luxury wellness studio leased 12,028 SF at 2 Gansevoort, Meatpacking District

stories.summary: LIV Method, a private luxury training and wellness studio, has signed a 12,028-square-foot lease at Sage's 2 Gansevoort Street in Manhattan's Meatpacking District, opening in January 2025. Average asking rent in the Meatpacking District near Washington Street and 14th Street is approximately $333 per square foot.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily relevance. Luxury wellness and fitness concept leasing in the Meatpacking District signals continued upmarket residential demand and high resident spending power in the submarket, reinforcing Meatpacking/West Village as a premium residential node. However, this is retail/amenity, not a meaningful employment driver or population inflection point for multifamily developers in the area.

stories.title: Elberon Joint Venture Breaks Ground on FreezPak Build-to-Suit
stories.excerpt: New Jersey-based Elberon Development Group and joint venture partner Saoud Development recently broke ground on a 146,000-square-foot cold storage facility on the corner of Amboy Avenue and South Front Street in Elizabeth, NJ, as a build-to-suit for FreezPak Logistics. It’s the second build-to-suit project for the JV and FreezPak’s seventh facility in its home state. “We are thrilled to be working alongside our friends at FreezPak on another state-of-the-art project,” said Elberon CEO Dave Gibbons. “Not only will the new facility accommodate FreezPak’s growing operations in New Jersey, but it also reinforces Elizabeth’s reputation as the premier industrial and logistics market in the Tri-State area.” The purpose-built facility will offer approximately 9.85 million cubic feet of temperature-controlled warehouse space as well as the full suite of services that FreezPak customers depend on, ranging from cold storage to USDA/FSIS inspections. It will be situated on an 8.3-acre cleared land site that Elberon and Saoud acquired from Phelps Dodge Industries in 2025. Delivery is expected in fourth quarter 2027. The post Elberon Joint Venture Breaks Ground on FreezPak Build-to-Suit appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Elberon and Saoud Development broke ground on 146K SF cold-storage build-to-suit in Elizabeth, NJ
FreezPak Logistics securing seventh facility in New Jersey; delivery Q4 2027
9.85M cubic feet temperature-controlled warehouse on 8.3-acre site; full USDA/FSIS capability
stories.summary: Elberon Development Group and joint venture partner Saoud Development broke ground on a 146,000-square-foot temperature-controlled cold-storage facility in Elizabeth, New Jersey, as a build-to-suit for FreezPak Logistics. The facility will provide approximately 9.85 million cubic feet of USDA/FSIS-compliant storage and logistics services. Expected delivery is Q4 2027. The site was cleared land acquired from Phelps Dodge Industries in 2025 on an 8.3-acre parcel at the corner of Amboy Avenue and South Front Street.
stories.impact: FreezPak's seventh New Jersey facility and Elizabeth's reinforcement as a premier Tri-State logistics hub signal ongoing distribution and cold-chain consolidation in the Newark–Elizabeth corridor. This drives demand for last-mile logistics workers, CDL drivers, and warehouse/distribution labor, typically middle-wage earners. Developers should assess multifamily sites within 10–15 minute commute of Elizabeth industrial clusters (particularly Port Newark, Ports Authority inland facilities, and Amboy Avenue logistics corridor) to capture wage-stable, benefits-seeking logistics worker cohorts. The Q4 2027 delivery timeline suggests a 2-year labor-inflow window requiring near-term multifamily start or acquisition.

stories.title: Forbright Bank Provides $50M for Southern California R&D Campus
stories.excerpt: The owners of a fully leased research and development and office campus in Thousand Oaks, Calif., have secured bridge financing after spending two years repositioning the asset. Los Angeles-based Alta West Partners closed the three-year, floating-rate loan of $49.8 million from Forbright Bank. JLL Capital Markets announced the financing Tuesday after representing the sponsor. The 275,000-square-foot Class A asset called Lakeview Innovation Center is on 22 acres in Ventura County. It includes lab space as well as office and R&D space, plus dock-high loading capabilities and 20,000 amps of electrical capacity. Alta West acquired the campus in September 2024, and through leasing and capital improvements generated more than 170 percent growth in net operating income, according to JLL. Tenants include semiconductor company Marvell, Laboratory Corporation of America, Rawlings Sporting Goods and Anchor Loans. The campus also features an Equinox fitness center, a full-service café, a two-story atrium, a pickleball court and 24-hour security. JLL’s team included Jeff Sause, Marc Schillinger, Josh Blank, Alex Olson, Jalynn Borders and Danny Ryan. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Forbright Bank financed $50M bridge loan for Lakeview Innovation Center, Thousand Oaks, CA
Alta West grew NOI 170% in 24 months; full occupancy with Marvell, LabCorp tenants
22-acre Class A R&D/office campus with 20K amps power, lab and dock-high loading
stories.summary: Forbright Bank closed a three-year, floating-rate bridge loan of $49.8 million for Lakeview Innovation Center, a fully leased 275,000-square-foot Class A R&D and office campus in Thousand Oaks, Ventura County, California. Alta West Partners, the sponsor, acquired the property in September 2024 at 50% occupancy and through 24 months of repositioning achieved full occupancy and more than 170% NOI growth. The 22-acre campus includes lab space, office, R&D, dock-high loading, 20,000 amps electrical capacity, and lifestyle amenities including Equinox, a café, and pickleball courts. Tenants include semiconductor firm Marvell, Laboratory Corporation of America, Rawlings Sporting Goods, and Anchor Loans.
stories.impact: Same as idx 2 (duplicate story); see prior analysis on Ventura County tech-sector clustering and multifamily adjacency opportunity in Thousand Oaks and regional submarkets.

stories.title: Design Firm Twelve Doubles HQ at Two Trees’ 45 Main Street to 14K SF
stories.excerpt: Design firm Twelve has upped its Brooklyn office headquarters by twofold. Twelve inked a 7,000-square-foot lease expansion at Dumbo’s 45 Main Street, according to a spokesperson for landlord Two Trees Management. The deal doubles Twelve’s office footprint to 14,000 square feet, spanning part of the 12-story office building’s sixth floor. The seven-year lease carried an asking rent of $52 per square foot. Crain’s New York first reported on the deal. Twelve, founded in 2005, produces merchandise and packaging for brands, and names Dior and the New York Times among its clients. In addition to its Dumbo base, the firm maintains global offices in Paris, London, Hong Kong and Shenzhen. Twelve did not work with a broker on the expansion. Two Trees was represented in-house by Alyssa Zahler and Elizabeth Bueno. “Twelve’s decision to double its footprint in Dumbo is a testament to the enduring appeal of the neighborhood as a home for creative businesses,” Bueno said in a statement. Prior to its decade-plus tenure at 45 Main Street, Twelve spent three years at Two Trees’ 55 Washington Street, located just around the corner. The firm arrived at Main Street in 2015 and increased its footprint there multiple times, according to Two Trees. Twelve’s move into another 7,000 square feet is expected to take place in the first quarter of 2027. “Doubling our space gives our incredible team more room to collaborate and spread their wings,” Katie Conovitz, founder and CEO of Twelve, said in a statement. “Equally important, the expansion allows us to continue hosting our incredible clients, with the ambition that each one leaves feeling inspired and energized.” The 476,000-square-foot office building on Main Street between Front and Water streets hosts a roster of design studios and other creative firms, including recent arrivals Church Edit, a film editing services collective, and Think! stories.summary: Design firm Twelve upped its Brooklyn headquarters by expanding 7,000 square feet at Two Trees Management's 45 Main Street in Dumbo, doubling its footprint to 14,000 square feet across part of the 12-story office building's sixth floor. The seven-year lease carried an asking rent of $52 per square foot. Twelve, founded in 2005, produces packaging and merchandise for global brands including Dior and the New York Times, and maintains offices in Paris, London, Hong Kong, and Shenzhen.
stories.impact: Twelve's expansion signals continued demand for creative-office space in Dumbo and reflects confidence in the submarket's creative-industry clustering and talent retention. The $52/SF asking rent (approx. $624/year all-in) and creative-sector occupation reinforce Dumbo as a high-wage employment node, driving demand for upmarket residential in adjacent Williamsburg, DUMBO proper, and Brooklyn Heights. Developers should note that creative-sector office growth (typically 15–25% wage premiums over metro average) supports market-rate or luxury multifamily development in pedestrian-accessible proximity. However, Dumbo's limited ground-up development capacity and historic-preservation constraints may favor adaptive-reuse or condo-heavy residential models over bulk rental delivery.

stories.title: AT&T Renews 7K-SF Lease at Rudin’s 3 Times Square
stories.excerpt: Home is where the heart is, and telecommunications giant at&t is quite at home in the heart of Times Square. The wireless carrier has renewed and extended its lease at Rudin’s 3 Times Square for another five years, Commercial Observer has learned. AT&T occupies 6,623 square feet of ground-floor and lower-level retail space at the 925,000-square-foot Midtown office tower. AT&T moved into the 30-story property, located on Seventh Avenue between West 42nd and West 43rd streets, in 2008. “Times Square remains one of the world’s most dynamic and heavily trafficked retail corridors in the world, and AT&T’s renewed commitment at 3 Times Square reinforces its spot at the center of it all,” Kevin Daly, vice president of commercial leasing at Rudin, said in a statement. Daly represented Rudin in-house alongside Craig Panzirer, senior vice president and head of office leasing at Rudin. The asking rent for the AT&T deal was not disclosed. The average asking rent for retail space in Times Square was $1,400 per square foot during the third quarter of 2026, according to CBRE data. The tenant was represented by Loren Baron from CBRE. Baron did not immediately respond to CO’s request for comment. “Extending our lease at 3 Times Square reflects AT&T’s long-term commitment to New York City and to serving customers in one of the world’s most vibrant commercial districts,” Keron Incarnato, AT&T’s vice president and general manager for the Northeast, said in a statement. “This location keeps us connected to the people, businesses and visitors who power the city, while giving customers a convenient place to explore the latest devices, services and connectivity solutions.” The AT&T extension follows Rudin’s April 2026 retail lease with jeweler Pandora, which took 4,107 square feet at 3 Times Square, CO reported in the spring. stories.summary: Telecommunications giant AT&T renewed and extended its lease at Rudin Management's 3 Times Square for another five years. AT&T occupies 6,623 square feet of ground-floor and lower-level retail space at the 925,000-square-foot Midtown office tower and has been a tenant since 2008. The average asking rent for retail space in Times Square was $1,400 per square foot during the third quarter of 2024. Lease terms and rent were not disclosed.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily relevance. AT&T's five-year renewal in Times Square reflects sustained retail activation and foot traffic in the submarket, supporting mixed-use and hotel-residential adjacency economics. However, this is a retail-lease renewal, not a material employment or population driver. Times Square's retail vibrancy supports premium residential valuations nearby (Hudson Yards, Chelsea, Midtown South), but the signal is incremental, not transformational.

stories.title: Brooklyn Powerhouse Sports to Open 11K-SF Facility in Sunset Park
stories.excerpt: Brooklyn Powerhouse Sports, a new fitness and athletic training facility, is opening its first location. Brooklyn Powerhouse has signed a 10,871-square-foot lease at Capstone Equities’ 14 53rd Street, known as the Whale Building, near the shore of New York Harbor in Sunset Park, Commercial Observer has learned. The company will set up batting cages and a small office at the location. The tenant will occupy space on the property’s third floor for eight years, at an asking rent of $28 per square foot, according to landlord broker Newmark. “This lease continues the transformation of the Whale Building into a destination for experiential and active tenants, joining Soccer Roof and the strong wave of leasing we’ve completed at the property,” Edward Kent of Capstone Equities said in a statement. “We’re excited to bring a new sports and entertainment offering to Sunset Park and the broader Brooklyn community.” Bernard Weitzman, Ryan Gessin, Jordan Gosin and Rohan Kapur from Newmark represented the landlord in this deal. The brokers declined to comment. Brooklyn Powerhouse’s new Sunset Park facility will feature dedicated spaces for baseball and softball training, including batting cages and tech simulators. “Opening Brooklyn Powerhouse Sports has been a dream of ours, and we’re proud to bring Brooklyn its premier batting cage facility,” Shamus Connolly, founder of Brooklyn Powerhouse Sports, said in a statement. “We’ve designed this space for players of all abilities — from kids taking their first swings to seasoned athletes working on their mechanics. We can’t wait to welcome the community.” The tenant was represented by Whitten Morris from JLL. “Brooklyn Powerhouse Sports had a very specific vision for its first facility, so finding the right space was especially important,” Morris said. “The property at 14 53rd Street offered the size and flexibility needed to bring that vision to life, while providing a strong foundation for the business a
bullets: Brooklyn Powerhouse Sports leased 10,871 SF at Capstone Equities' 14 53rd Street, Sunset Park
Eight-year lease at $28/SF in Whale Building, third floor; batting cages and office
Capstone transforming Whale Building into destination for experiential/active tenants
stories.summary: Brooklyn Powerhouse Sports, a new fitness and athletic training facility, signed a 10,871-square-foot lease at Capstone Equities' 14 53rd Street (the Whale Building) in Sunset Park, near the shore of New York Harbor. The company will set up batting cages and a small office on the property's third floor for eight years at an asking rent of $28 per square foot. This is Powerhouse's first location. Capstone is positioning the Whale Building as a destination for experiential and active tenants, alongside existing tenant Soccer Roof.
stories.impact: Experiential and fitness concept tenancy at $28/SF in industrial-converted Sunset Park signals emerging consumer-facing mixed-use activation in the submarket, typically a precursor to residential densification. Sunset Park's waterfront-adjacent location, affordability relative to Carroll Gardens and Park Slope, and improving transit (Brooklyn-Queens Greenway) are attracting young, active-lifestyle tenants and positioning the submarket for middle-market to workforce multifamily inflow. Developers should monitor Whale Building cluster and similar industrial-to-experience conversions as leading indicators of residential demand inflection; Sunset Park's affordability and waterfront access position it as a prime target for 150–200-unit garden-style and mid-rise development within 3–5 years if experiential tenant clustering continues.
